conceptName: Integers: Positive and Negative Numbers on a Number Line
subject: Mathematics
author: SahaayaLearn Academic Team
learningObjective: Understand negative integers as directional opposites of positive numbers and apply them on a number line.
simpleExplanation: Integers include all positive counting numbers, zero, and their negative opposites. Negative numbers represent values below zero, like colder temperatures or debts.
detailedExplanation: On a horizontal number line, zero sits at the center. Numbers to the right of zero are positive (+1, +2, +3...) and get larger as you move right. Numbers to the left of zero are negative (-1, -2, -3...) and get smaller as you move left. Notice that -5 is smaller than -2 because -5 is further to the left.
everydayExample: Imagine an elevator in a Bengaluru hospital building. Ground floor is 0. 1st, 2nd, and 3rd floors are +1, +2, +3. The basement parking levels underground are -1, -2, -3. If you are at -2, you are two floors below the ground!

commonMisconceptions.description: Assuming -10 is greater than -2 because 10 is greater than 2.
commonMisconceptions.diagnosticQuestion: Is owing 10 rupees to a friend better or worse than owing 2 rupees?
commonMisconceptions.correctionStrategy: Clarify that more negative means lower on the number line: -10 is colder and smaller than -2.

practiceQuestions.question: Which integer is greater: -3 or -8?
practiceQuestions.explanation: -3 is to the right of -8 on the number line, so -3 is greater than -8.
